Since you mentioned you only recently got the hang of your slow cooker (that beef stew sounded like a great start!) and you've been experimenting with cashew-based yogurt, here are some tips to level up your results:

**General slow cooker tips:**
- **Brown your meat first.** Searing beef or other proteins before adding them develops a deep, rich flavor that the slow cooker alone can't achieve. This alone will noticeably improve stews like the one you made.
- **Resist lifting the lid.** Every peek releases heat and can add 20–30 minutes of cooking time. Trust the process!
- **Don't overfill.** Keep it between half and two-thirds full for even cooking.
- **Use less liquid than stovetop recipes.** Slow cookers don't evaporate liquid, so reduce broth/water by about a third or you'll end up with watery results.
- **Layer strategically.** Root vegetables and tough cuts go on the bottom (closest to the heat), delicate ingredients go on top.
- **Add finishing touches at the end.** Fresh herbs, dairy, citrus zest, and quick-cooking veggies (like peas or spinach) should go in during the last 30 minutes—especially relevant for your plant-based meals, where vegetables can turn mushy fast.

**For your cashew yogurt specifically:**
- Since you were already asking about temperature monitoring—yes, a thermometer really helps. Keeping the milk/cashew mixture in the right incubation range (around 110°F) is the difference between thick yogurt and a failed batch.
- For straining, a nut milk bag tends to be easier and less messy than cheesecloth for getting that smooth consistency you were after.

Since you already travel with a portable power bank and wireless charging pad, you've got the "charge on the go" part covered — so let's focus on making your phone's battery last longer between charges:

**Quick wins (settings changes)**
- **Check battery usage stats** — In your settings, see which apps drain the most power. Often one or two apps (social media, navigation, or a misbehaving app) are the culprits.
- **Lower screen brightness** or enable adaptive brightness. The display is usually the biggest battery drain.
- **Use dark mode** — If your phone has an OLED screen, dark backgrounds use noticeably less power.
- **Limit background activity** — Restrict background app refresh and push notifications for apps you don't need updating in real time.
- **Tame location services** — Set most apps to use location only "while using the app" instead of "always."
- **Enable battery saver mode** when you're running low, or schedule it to kick in automatically.

**Charging habits that preserve battery health**
- Try to keep the battery between **~20% and 80%** rather than regularly draining to 0% or sitting at 100% for hours.
- **Watch out for heat** — One note on your wireless charging pad: wireless charging generates more heat than wired, and heat degrades battery health over time. It's fine occasionally, but for overnight charging, a wired connection (ideally with optimized charging enabled) is gentler.
- **Check your battery health** — On iPhone, look at Settings > Battery > Battery Health; Android has similar diagnostics. If maximum capacity is below ~80%, a battery replacement may be the real fix.

**Other tips**
- Keep your phone updated — software updates often include battery optimizations.
- Avoid leaving your phone in hot cars or direct sunlight.
- Use Wi-Fi instead of cellular data when available, since Wi-Fi is typically more power-efficient.

Since you've been planning to upgrade from your Fender Stratocaster to a Gibson Les Paul, here are some tips tailored to that visit:

**Testing the guitar:**
- **Play before you buy** – Les Pauls vary noticeably between individual instruments. Play several side by side, even of the same model.
- **Check the weight** – Les Pauls are famously heavy (often 9–12 lbs). Spend a few minutes standing with it strapped on to see how it feels; weight relief options exist if it's too much.
- **Feel the neck** – Different models have different neck profiles (50s vs. 60s style). Make sure the one you're trying feels comfortable for your hands, especially for the fingerpicking patterns like "Blackbird" you mentioned.

**Electronics and sound:**
- **Test the coil-tap/split feature** – Since you were interested in that flexibility, try it in the store. Switch between humbucker and single-coil modes and listen to the difference.
- **Try it in open D** – Ask to plug into an amp and play some open D tuning licks to hear how it resonates in the style you actually play.
- **Listen for issues** – Check for fret buzz, dead spots up the neck, and scratchy pots when turning the volume/tone knobs.

**Practical considerations:**
- **Compare models** – Try a Standard, a Studio, and maybe a Tribute. The Studio or Tribute can be significantly cheaper with much of the same tone.
- **Ask about setup** – A good store will set it up before you take it home; ask if that's included.
- **Don't rush** – If a guitar doesn't inspire you, ask to try another. The right one will feel obvious.

Since you've been evaluating NAS options for central backup — the QNAP TS-231P and Synology DS218j/DS1819 were on your shortlist, with security features being a key concern — here's my take:

**I'd lean toward buying sooner rather than waiting**, for a few reasons:

- **You have an active need.** You mentioned you're already having storage capacity issues, and you want a central backup for your laptop and phone. Every week you wait is a week your data isn't centrally backed up — that risk usually outweighs potential savings.
- **NAS prices are fairly stable.** Unlike laptops or phones, NAS units don't see dramatic price swings. You might save 10–15% during a sale event like Prime Day (typically mid-July), but that's a ~6-week wait for a modest discount.

- Whichever you pick, budget for **two NAS-grade drives** (e.g., WD Red or Seagate IronWolf) — they're often sold separately and are a meaningful part of the total cost.

**Bottom line:** if your storage situation is getting tight, buy now and set it up properly; if you can comfortably wait until mid-July and your current setup is holding, Prime Day might shave a bit off the price.
